moments.title: Five ships
moments.text: The Trinidad, San Antonio, Concepción, Victoria and Santiago leave Sanlúcar with about 260 men. Magellan, a Portuguese captain sailing for Spain, has told his crews little of where they are going.

moments.title: The bay of Santa Lucía
moments.text: In the bay that will become Rio de Janeiro the crews trade with the Tupi people, who have had no rain for two months and greet the fleet with rain falling. Pigafetta fills pages with what he sees.

moments.title: Not a strait
moments.text: The great opening in the coast that Magellan hoped was the passage west is only the mouth of a river, the Río de la Plata. The search moves south into colder water.

moments.title: Mutiny at San Julián
moments.text: Wintering in a bleak harbor, three of the five captains rise against Magellan. He retakes the ships within a day; one captain is executed and another left marooned when the fleet sails.

moments.title: The Tehuelche
moments.text: Tall men dressed in guanaco skins come to the shore. The Europeans call them Patagones, giants. Magellan has two of them seized by trickery to take to Spain.

moments.title: The strait
moments.text: Past a cape they name for the Eleven Thousand Virgins, a channel opens westward. For five weeks the ships thread a maze of fjords between snowy mountains. At night they see fires burning on the land to the south.

moments.title: The San Antonio turns back
moments.text: The largest ship, with most of the fleet's food, slips away in the strait and sails home to Spain. Magellan does not know where she has gone.

moments.title: The Pacific
moments.text: Three ships come out of the strait into an open ocean so calm that they call it the Pacific. It is far wider than any chart showed.

moments.title: An empty island
moments.text: After two months of open sea they find a small uninhabited island with no anchorage and call it San Pablo. Which atoll it was is still argued.

moments.title: Ninety-eight days
moments.text: The biscuit is powder full of worms, the water is yellow and stinking, and men eat the leather off the yards and sawdust and rats. Scurvy kills nineteen men or more.

moments.title: Guam
moments.text: Chamorro people paddle out in fast outrigger canoes and take what they want from the ships, by their own ideas of exchange. Magellan answers by burning houses and killing seven men, and names the islands for thieves.

moments.title: Enrique speaks
moments.text: At Limasawa, Magellan's enslaved servant Enrique, taken in Malacca years before, calls out to the people in a canoe, and they understand him. Language has come around the world before any ship has.

moments.title: Mactan
moments.text: Determined to force the island of Mactan to submit, Magellan wades ashore with a small party and is killed in the shallows by Lapulapu's warriors.

moments.title: The banquet at Cebu
moments.text: Invited to a feast by the ruler of Cebu, more than twenty of the officers are killed. Too few men are left for three ships, and the Concepción is burned.

moments.title: The Spice Islands
moments.text: Twenty-seven months after leaving Spain, the two remaining ships anchor at Tidore and fire their guns for joy. The sultan welcomes them, and they load cloves.

moments.title: One ship west
moments.text: The Trinidad is leaking and stays behind for repairs. Juan Sebastián Elcano sails the Victoria west for Spain, across the Indian Ocean, away from Portuguese ports.

moments.title: The Cape
moments.text: For weeks contrary gales hold the Victoria back from rounding the Cape of Good Hope. The men are starving, and some want to give in and sail for Mozambique.

moments.title: The missing day
moments.text: Ashore at Cape Verde for food, the men learn it is Thursday. By the careful count Pigafetta has kept, it is Wednesday. Sailing west with the sun, they have lost a day.

moments.title: Eighteen men
moments.text: The Victoria comes back into Sanlúcar, nearly three years after leaving it, with eighteen of her crew. They are the first people known to have sailed all the way around the world.
